items.text: Both spectra show G (near 1580 cm-1) and 2D (near 2680 to 2700 cm-1), confirming graphene on both metals
items.locator: Bukvisova 2025 main text p.3 ('we have confirmed that the layers ... are graphene'), Fig. S1D

items.text: The D peak (near 1345 to 1350 cm-1) is relatively stronger on Au (I_D/I_G about 1 by peak height) than on Cu (about 0.6, poorly constrained because the Cu signal is weak)
items.locator: Fig. S1D caption ('Higher intensity D peak ... on Au'); ratio measured by the curator

items.text: Reports the authors' explanation: the stronger D on Au is likely related to strain from the rapid solidification of the droplet, and labels it as their hypothesis

Points out that the D band needs a defect (or edge) to be activated, so a strong D means more Raman-active defects or domain edges in the spot; strain by itself shifts G and 2D, and a strain explanation should be checked against the G and 2D positions

Rev. B 79, 205433, arXiv:0812.1538 (strain shifts G and 2D)

items.text: Asks for the laser wavelength, needed for any L_D estimate (I_D/I_G scales with lambda^4) and for comparing 2D positions (2D disperses with excitation energy)
items.locator: Cancado, Jorio, Martins Ferreira, Stavale, Achete, Capaz, Moutinho, Lombardo, Kulmala, Ferrari 2011, Quantifying defects in graphene via Raman spectroscopy at different excitation energies, Nano Lett. 11, 3190, doi:10.1021/nl201432g, arXiv:1105.0175 Eq. 4 and p.5

items.text: The Cu spectrum has a much weaker signal, so its D/G ratio and peak widths are poorly constrained; comparisons need error bars or longer integration
items.locator: measured (Cu G height about 25 counts over a noise of about 9)

wrong_claims.text: Gives a quantitative L_D or defect density without knowing the laser wavelength
States as established fact that the D peak on Au is caused by strain

notes: Experimental, unchanged except for dropping shifts below 100 cm-1 and sorting x ascending. The paper states only what items f1 and f3 and the caption say; it gives no laser wavelength, no layer number and no peak positions. Curator fits (Lorentzians on a linear baseline): Au D 1344.4, G 1580.3, 2D 2681.1 cm-1, D/G heights 111/117 about 0.95, 2D/G about 2.9; Cu G about 1580 to 1587 (height about 22 to 26 counts, noise sd about 9), 2D 2695.7 (height about 50), D weak (about 14 counts, poorly constrained). The Au spectrum is also used by the identification case dev/exp-graphene-01.
